blocks.text: 07-LPG / landing pages and funnels Goes here. A breakdown of a three-pillar framework for building high-converting landing pages: Offer/Copywriting, Design Structure, and Iterative A/B Testing. Covers Voice of Customer research, the PAS (Problem-Agitate-Solve) copywriting framework, and specific layout sections (Hero, Pain Point, Social Proof, Value Props). Not here. • Paid media campaign setup or top-of-funnel traffic generation -> 06-MEA • Automated email marketing flows -> 09-EML

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Provides a strategic, three-pillar framework for diagnosing and rebuilding underperforming landing pages, detailing how to extract Voice of Customer data and translate it into specific copywriting formulas and visual layouts. modules: [LPG] topics: [landing page design, conversion rate optimization, CRO, copywriting, problem-agitate-solve, above the fold, social proof, A/B testing, user research, Microsoft Clarity] tier: 3 scope_hint: comprehensive

Topics. diagnosing landing page failures / identifying that simply checking boxes (adding random reviews or generic pain points) without a cohesive, offer-driven strategy results in wasted ad spend; the three-pillar landing page system / outlining the framework: (1) Offer & Copywriting derived from deep research, (2) High-Converting Design built around that copy, and (3) Iterative A/B Testing; Voice of Customer (VoC) research / utilizing Reddit, sales team interviews, and qualitative testing tools (UserBrain) to harvest exact customer phrasing, pain points, and objections before writing a single word of copy; crafting the hero section / using the formula "[End Result] + [Time Period] + [Emotional Payoff]" for the main headline, and the "Stop doing X, no more Y [pain] -> Our solution does Z [benefit]" formula for the sub-headline; reducing FUDs / mitigating Fear, Uncertainty, and Doubt directly beneath the Call to Action button (e.g., "Cancel anytime," "100% Guaranteed") to immediately lower perceived risk; executing the pain point section / utilizing the Problem-Agitate-Solve (PAS) framework for long-form sales letters on complex offers, versus using scannable visual comparisons (e.g., "Old Way vs. New Way") for transformative/visual offers; social proof strategies / abandoning generic "Our Reviews" headers in favor of benefit-driven titles (e.g., "Helping 110,000 members achieve [Dream Outcome]") and utilizing "Walls of Love" that blend video and text testimonials with clear source attribution; feature-to-benefit translation / requiring that all value propositions answer the "So What?" question until the core benefit is reached, and ensuring that benefit is explicitly stated in the section headline (since 80% of users only scan); the necessity of continuous CRO / emphasizing that the landing page that gets a business to $1M will not get them to $10M without continuous iteration using tools like Microsoft Clarity (heatmaps/recordings), Google Analytics, and A/B testing platforms (Intelligems, Go Stellar).

The "So What?" Feature-to-Benefit Translation: A copywriting technique that takes a product feature and repeatedly asks "So what?" to drill down to the ultimate customer benefit (e.g., Feature: "Clear reports" -> So what? -> "Make smarter decisions" -> So what? -> Benefit: "Grow your bottom line").

The Problem-Agitate-Solve (PAS) Framework: A copywriting structure for the "Pain Point" section where you identify the struggle, agitate the emotional consequences of that struggle, and then introduce the product as the clear solution.

The "Wall of Love" Social Proof Layout: The design strategy of inundating the user with a dense grid of mixed media (video reviews, text reviews, before/after photos) that clearly displays the verifiable source (e.g., Google, Trustpilot) to instantly build massive credibility.
The Hero Headline Formula: The specific copywriting framework for the main headline: "[End Result] + [Time Period] + [Emotional Payoff]" (e.g., "Get 20/20 Vision in 10 Minutes and Feel Safe").
Skip. Plugs for the creator's swipe file, generic lists of client ROI percentages without strategic context, and the outro teasing the next video.
Scope mix. 15% baseline (basic definitions of landing page sections), 85% growth (advanced copywriting formulas, VoC research techniques, and UX design frameworks). Volume. ~400 words.
